title: Prajnya document JSON
description: One file per processed PDF: run_outputs/documents/<name>.v6.json. This schema pins the part other programs may rely on. Keys it does not name (for example pages[].metadata.analysis) are internal and may change in any release. Unknown extra keys are always allowed, so adding a key is never a breaking change. See contract/README.md for the version rules.

if.$comment: A file that says it follows contract 1.1 or later must carry the citations block. Files from contract 1.0 (or with no version stamp) have none.

allOf.$comment: Each rule below: a file that says it follows contract 1.N or later must carry what 1.N added. The if/then above does the same for 1.1 (citations). A file older than the rule, or with no version stamp, is not held to it.
Contract 1.3 added each page's body, furniture and outside_body.

status.description: Contract 1.5. Whether the document really finished. "success": every page was read. "partial": written, but the pages in `failed_pages` failed (a failed page keeps its text layer when it has one; its figures and tables are lost); such a document is not recorded as processed and is tried again on the next run. "failed": the strategy stopped with an error (see `summary.errors`), or no page came out. `success` keeps its old meaning (no strategy error), so a partial document can say `success: true`. Absent in files older than 1.5.

failed_pages.description: Contract 1.5. The 1-based numbers of the pages whose reading failed; [] when none did. Absent in files older than 1.5.

pipeline_version.description: The Prajnya release that wrote this file.

contract_version.description: The version of THIS contract the file follows. Absent in files written by Prajnya 6.3.0 or earlier, which follow contract 1.0 in every respect except that they do not say so.

author_names.description: Contract 1.4. The same authors with the surname apart, one entry per name in `authors`, in the same order; each `family` ends its author's string in `authors`. [] when no registry record gave surnames (levels local and zotero, an OpenAlex record, a hand-corrected list). Absent in files older than 1.4.

doi.description: Bare DOI, '10.xxxx/...', with no URL prefix.

pages.description: One entry per processed page, in page order.

profile.description: The un-flattened internal record. Only the two members named here are part of the contract.

pdf_path.$comment: Informational only. This is an ABSOLUTE path on the machine that ran Prajnya. Never open it, never publish it, never rely on it being present.

review_status.description: Present once the metadata review step has run.

citations.description: How to cite this document, and how that was established. Present in every file from contract 1.1 on, at every level. Since contract 1.1.

level.description: The run setting. 'local': Prajnya's own reading of the PDF, nothing left the machine. 'zotero': checked against the researcher's Zotero library. 'online': Crossref / OpenAlex; only this level can carry references and markers.

level_set_by.description: What decided the level: the --citations flag, citations.level in the config, an older config's zotero block, or nothing (the default, 'local').

metadata_source.description: Which step actually supplied metadata_final. 'extracted' is Prajnya's own reading. 'user' is a hand correction. 'file_name' means nothing usable was found (see cited_by_file_name). The level says what was allowed; this says what happened.

source_label.description: The short form to cite the document by: 'Bella, 2016', 'Fullerton et al., 2006', 'Halper (ed.), 2021'. Derived from metadata_final. When cited_by_file_name is true it is the PDF's file name.

cited_by_file_name.description: true when no author, editor or title was usable. The file name is then in source_label ONLY; metadata_final.title stays null. Such a document needs a human.

network.description: Level 'online' only: whether the services could be reached. Absent at the other levels.

status.description: 'not_requested': the level does not fetch lists (local, zotero). 'found': references holds it. 'not_available': asked, and no service holds one. 'not_reached': the network failed, so nothing is known.

source.description: Where the entries came from, when found.

style.description: How the paper prints its list.

local_count.description: Entries Prajnya's own splitter counted in the PDF, an independent second reading. null when the splitter could not read the list.

counts_agree.description: Whether count and local_count are equal. null when local_count is null.

references.description: The paper's own reference list, in printed order. Empty unless reference_list.status is 'found'.

markers.description: In-text citation marks linked to references. Empty unless the list passed its checks: a wrong link is worse than none.

position.description: Place in printed order, from 1. Always present.

number.description: The number as PRINTED in a numbered list ('[245]' cites number 245). null in an author-year list.

container.description: The journal or book the cited work appeared in.

doi.description: Bare DOI of the CITED work, when known.

printed_text.description: The entry as printed in the PDF, when Prajnya's splitter read it.

mentions.description: In-text figure and table mentions ('Fig. 3B', 'Table 2'), linked to the figure and table objects that carry that printed label. Derived from the page text on every write, at every citation level. Since contract 1.2.

figures.description: Mentions of main-text figures, in page and reading order.

tables.description: Mentions of tables, in page and reading order.

skipped.description: How many mentions were found and deliberately NOT linked.

supplementary.description: 'Figure S1', 'Supplementary Fig. 3', 'S1 Fig', 'Extended Data Fig. 2', 'Figure 2-figure supplement 1': not printed in the article.

own_label.description: A legend's own label ('Figure 3.' starting Figure 3's caption).

kind.description: placeholder: Prajnya's [[FIGURE ...]] / [[TABLE ...]] lines and <!-- --> comments. table: a table written as HTML or as a Markdown grid. caption: a figure or table legend, where the page text holds the legend stored on that object. reference_list: from the References heading to the end of the list (a heading that follows reference lists, a legend, or the next book chapter); text after the list, such as Cell Press STAR Methods or eLife appendices, is body.

start.description: Where the part starts in the page's content.

kind.description: running_line: a running header or footer (journal line, author short names, a folio line). page_number: a line that is only the printed page number. Header and footer are not told apart: a text-layer page often writes its header at the end.

start.description: Where the line starts in the page's content.

end.description: Where the line ends in content, its line break excluded.

content_offset.description: Character offset in that page's content string: where the mention starts, or for a later number in it ('Figures 2 and 3'), where that number stands.

text.description: The whole mention as printed, whitespace collapsed: 'Figures 3A and 4'.

number.description: The ONE printed number this record links: '4', '11.1', 'II'. A mention naming two figures gives two records; panels of one figure ('Fig 1A and 1D') give one.

targets.description: The figure_id / table_id of every object carrying that label (a figure split into several crops has several). Empty when no object with that label was found: the mention is real, the object is missing.

text.description: The mark as printed: '[3-7]', '12,14', 'Doi et al., 2005', 'Berendsen (1962)'.

numbers.description: The references it cites, as the `position`s of those references in `references` (1-based). For a numbered list a linked reference's position equals its printed number, so '[3-7]' gives 3..7 (ranges expanded); for an author-year list, a mark names its references by author and year and the list decides which entries they are.

context_before.description: The text just before the mark, to find it again.

content_offset.description: Character offset of the mark in that page's content string. null when it could not be found there exactly once.

content.description: The page text, as Markdown. On a model-read page it is the model's reading; on a text-layer page it is the PDF's own text.

body.description: From contract 1.3. The page's running text: content without its furniture lines (metadata.furniture) and the parts listed in metadata.outside_body (placeholders, tables, legends, the reference list). Whole lines go with their line breaks; every other character is as in content. For splitting text into passages. Every offset in the file (markers' and mentions' content_offset, furniture start/end) indexes content, never body.

quality_score.description: A rough guess from simple checks (text length, Markdown structure, odd characters, expected fields present), or a fixed value on some routes. Not a measured accuracy, and nothing in Prajnya acts on it; see contract/README.md rule 20.

processing_method.description: What ACTUALLY produced this page's text. 'pymupdf' is the historical name of the text-layer route and is kept for compatibility: the text layer is now read with pypdfium2. 'glm_failed' and 'two_shot_title_failed' mean the read FAILED; metadata.error then holds the reason and content is not a reliable reading. Absent on a book's front-matter pages (a known gap).

page_type.description: What the page classifier PREDICTED before reading. Where it and processing_method disagree, processing_method is the truth. null on title pages.

error.description: Present when the page failed; see processing_method.

furniture.description: From contract 1.3. The page's running headers, footers and page numbers, LABELLED and left in content (they carry the journal, volume and DOI). Found from the text alone: a line at the start or end of the page text that repeats on many pages, or whose number rises with the page. Empty when none was found; model-read pages mostly leave furniture out already.

outside_body.description: From contract 1.3. The other parts of content that are not running text and are left out of body, in text order, never overlapping. Each is kept elsewhere in the file (legends and tables on their objects, references under citations) or is Prajnya's own markup. Empty when there is none.

caption.description: May be empty or wrong: caption capture is a known open weakness.

printed_label.description: The label as printed, e.g. 'Fig. 9'. null when none was found.

label_key.description: The label normalised so crops of one printed figure share it.

panel_group_size.description: How many crops share this figure's label.

grid.description: The table rebuilt as rows and cells, written as an HTML <table> string. A cell's text may contain LaTeX math between $...$ delimiters (e.g. '$R_{\mathrm{b}}(\mathrm{s}^{-1})$'); a consumer must treat that as math markup, not as prose. Cell text is a model's reading and can contain errors.

size_ratio.description: Cap height relative to the body text.

authors.description: THIS chapter's authors, not the book's editors.

start_page_printed.description: The page number as PRINTED in the book, not a PDF page.

page_range.description: [first, last] PDF pages, 0-BASED, unlike pages[].page_number which is 1-based. Add 1 to each to get page numbers. null when the chapter's boundary was not found (2 of the 17 chapters in the corpus book); the key itself may also be absent.

bbox_page_pixels.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PIXELS of the page image Prajnya rendered for detection (not PDF points). Origin top-left.

bbox_pdf_points.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PDF POINTS (1/72 inch). A different unit from figure and table boxes in the same file.
